title: Why AI isn't replacing devs yet: the 3 AM test, environment context, and accountability
summary: Priyam argues AI is great at writing code but weak at the tribal knowledge, environment context, and accountability that keep a product alive. He runs a $1M ARR AI SaaS with an AI agent and still pays his dev team. The real risk is devs who don't learn AI tools.

principles.text: AI excels at writing code but fails at the context needed to keep a product running.
principles.quote: AI is incredible at writing code. It's terrible at everything else that actually keeps a product alive.

principles.text: Production incidents need someone with undocumented tribal knowledge of the system, which AI agents lack today.
principles.quote: That tribal knowledge lives in your developer's brain. And it's worth more than any AI can generate.

principles.text: AI fixes can be dangerous without environment context; devs who've been burned before catch these errors.
principles.quote: I've watched AI assistants confidently suggest fixes that would have nuked our production database. Not because the code was wrong - because the context was wrong.

principles.text: Humans provide accountability to customers when things break; AI cannot.
principles.quote: It doesn't feel the weight of a mistake and make sure it never happens again.

principles.text: AI is currently a multiplier for good developers rather than a replacement.
principles.quote: Right now, AI isn't replacing developers. It's making good developers faster.

principles.text: People get displaced by peers who adopt new tools, so learn AI now before the window closes.
principles.quote: The devs who get replaced first aren't losing their jobs to AI. They're losing them to other devs who learned AI tools.
